phases.name: 1. Foundations
phases.purpose: Transformer, pretraining, scaling, data, and decoder-only LLM progression.

phases.name: 2. Modern Block Anatomy
phases.purpose: RMSNorm, SwiGLU, RoPE, MQA/GQA: the internals of a modern LLM block.

phases.name: 3. Adaptation & Alignment
phases.purpose: Instruction tuning, PEFT, RLHF and preference optimization.

phases.name: 4. Training & Inference Systems
phases.purpose: Parallel training, kernels, serving, KV cache, decoding and quantization.

phases.name: 5. Retrieval, Agents & Reasoning
phases.purpose: RAG, tool use, verifiers, GRPO and test-time compute.

phases.name: 6. Sparse, Frontier & Alternative Architectures
phases.purpose: MoE, MLA, modern training systems, reasoning RL, SSMs and optimizers.

guidance: Follow Suggested Order unless a project gives you a reason to jump.
Deep-read Core papers; skim model reports and optional comparisons.
For systems papers, reproduce the central memory/FLOP/communication idea.
Use Status + Notes on the Paper Roadmap sheet as a live tracker.
Direct PDF URL is the download link; Paper Page URL is useful for metadata/version history.

phases.name: 1. Vision Foundations
phases.purpose: Acquire the modern CV vocabulary: CNNs, segmentation, detection and vision Transformers.

phases.name: 2. Self-Supervised & Foundation Vision
phases.purpose: Learn representation learning before EO-specific foundation models.

phases.name: 3. Matching, Registration & Motion
phases.purpose: Build the core toolkit for correspondence, local warps and sub-pixel registration.

phases.name: 4. EO Data & Multimodal Pretraining
phases.purpose: Move from generic vision to satellite-specific multimodal and multi-temporal representation learning.

phases.name: 5. SAR-Specific Learning
phases.purpose: Respect speckle, complex data, acquisition geometry and radar-specific inductive biases.

phases.name: 6. Temporal / Next-Scene Prediction
phases.purpose: Establish strong baselines for T-k → T+1 forecasting before inventing new models.

phases.name: 7. Physics-Aware ML
phases.purpose: Learn how to encode physical knowledge as constraints, architectures or hybrid models.

guidance: Do not wait to finish all vision papers before touching SAR.
Read phases 1–2 selectively, then work phase 3 in parallel with your co-registration prototype.
Phases 4–5 are the highest-value research layer for cross-mission SAR/EO.
For next-scene prediction, keep a strict baseline ladder: persistence → ConvLSTM → SimVP → Transformer.
Physics-aware means more than PINNs: use acquisition metadata, geometry, complex signal structure, invariances and hybrid residual models.
This workbook intentionally does not repeat the 54 LLM/system papers.

phases.name: 1. Domain Language & Data
phases.purpose: Learn what changes when text, labels, corpora and language are domain-specific.

phases.name: 2. Reasoning & Evaluation
phases.purpose: Evaluate legal competence instead of relying on generic benchmark scores.

phases.name: 3. Financial Language & Reasoning
phases.purpose: Learn numerical reasoning, filings and evidence-grounded finance QA.

phases.name: 4. Explainability, Confidence & Abstention
phases.purpose: Make confidence, uncertainty and escalation explicit.

phases.name: 5. Documentation, Fairness & Privacy
phases.purpose: Build evidence for transparency, fairness, data governance and privacy.

phases.name: 6. Governance & Operational Controls
phases.purpose: Translate model behavior into controls, accountability and regulated operations.

guidance: 1) Do phases 1–3 selectively by your target domain.
2) Do phases 4–6 regardless of domain: regulated AI is not just a better model.
3) For every Core item, produce an artifact: benchmark result, risk/control map, model card, or reproducible notebook.
4) The goal is evidence-backed deployment: provenance, calibration, abstention, privacy, fairness, human oversight and auditability.
5) This workbook intentionally does not repeat the 54 LLM/system papers.

phases.name: 1. Math Refresh
phases.purpose: Fill only genuine math gaps; do not turn prerequisite study into an endless delay.

phases.name: 2. Deep Learning Core
phases.purpose: Build from-scratch understanding and modern DL intuition alongside DeepML.

phases.name: 3. Computer Vision
phases.purpose: Acquire the visual/geometry toolkit needed before deep SAR specialization.

phases.name: 4. GPU & AI Systems
phases.purpose: Develop the hardware-aware ML layer: profiling, memory, kernels, serving and production reliability.

phases.name: 5. SAR & Earth Observation
phases.purpose: Learn radar physics, mission/product semantics and EO-specific modeling.

phases.name: 6. Regulated / Trustworthy AI
phases.purpose: Add interpretability, legal reasoning and evaluation/governance thinking.

phases.name: 7. Practical Consolidation
phases.purpose: Use broad practical courses only to close gaps or accelerate implementation.

guidance: Use at most 3 active learning resources at once:
1) one foundation stream (DeepML / math / DL),
2) one active-domain stream (SAR/CV or regulated AI),
3) one systems stream (GPU / production).
For every ~3–5 hours of reading/watching, spend ~3–5 hours implementing, deriving or benchmarking. Books marked Reference are not homework.

Downstream gain; phase sensitivity; compute/memory cost; interpretability

reg.Success Evidence: Evidence precision/recall; answer correctness; unsupported-claim rate; abstention quality

reg.Build: Clause extraction + NLI + evidence highlighting with mandatory human approval.
reg.Success Evidence: Clause F1; evidence span F1; calibration; review time saved

reg.Build: Financial report QA with retriever, executable numerical verifier and source citations.
reg.Success Evidence: Retrieval recall; execution accuracy; citation accuracy; hallucination rate

reg.Build: Produce model card, dataset datasheet, calibration/fairness tests, privacy test and governance mapping.
Tool-using agent with least privilege, human checkpoints, audit logs, deterministic controls and rollback.
reg.Success Evidence: Unsafe action rate; approval bypass rate; audit completeness; recovery time
